subject: SIG: MedArc network evidence - private endpoint / peering details
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@medarc.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: it-security@medarc.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: network evidence for private endpoints and peering

Hi Diego / Laura,

Thanks for the SIG draft so far. Our SecOps team is wrapping up the network section and has two items remaining that we need from Redwood to close the loop for our procurement review:

1) A concise list (CSV or plain text) of the egress IPs/CIDRs we should allow for calls originating from Redwood-managed private endpoints (for customers using Private deployment). Ideally the list should indicate whether each IP is static (S) or ephemeral (E), and the associated purpose (control plane, telemetry, KV cache).

2) A simple one-page topology diagram or PDF showing how a MedArc VPC would peer or connect to Redwood Private including DNS/flow direction for PrivateLink or VPC Peering options. We don't need a full architecture whitepaper — a clear diagram + callouts is enough.

Also: do you have a snapshot of the actual VPC peering config (security group / route table examples or export) you can share as a redacted text file? That would help our network engineers verify routes.

Target is to get this by EOD Monday (Apr 5) so we can close the SIG answers. If there are any constraints (eg. no static egress IPs for a given region) please call that out.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhao
Senior Security Engineer, MedArc Health
emily.zhao@medarc.com

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@medarc.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:08:14 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence for private endpoints and peering

Emily — thanks for the clarity, happy to provide. Quick answers up front, followed by attachments and clarifying questions.

Summary (high level)
- We can provide a maintained list of egress IPs by region. For most Private deployments we offer both static (reserved NAT/egress) options and ephemeral NAT pools depending on customer preference and contract.
- Attached: a CSV with the initial egress ranges we currently use in us-west-2 and us-east-1, a PDF topology diagram, and a text snapshot of peering config examples (routes/security groups redacted where appropriate).

Clarifying Qs
- Do you require a single /24 per region, or is a small set of CIDRs acceptable? Our reserved egress typically ships as at least a /29- /24 depending on region and capacity commitment.
- For PrivateLink customers (AWS PrivateLink / interface ENIs) we can provide the flow diagram showing DNS override patterns; however, those flows assume your side accepts interface endpoints rather than transit gw. Which approach is MedArc planning to use?

I'm attaching: redwood_private_endpoint_ip_allowlist_v1.csv (egress ranges + static/ephemeral flags), network_topology_medarc_private_endpoints_v1.pdf, vpc_peering_config_snapshot-20270405.txt.

If useful, I can also paste the minimal route table snippet inline.

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@medarc.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: it-security@medarc.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:31:27 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence for private endpoints and peering

Diego — thanks for the prompt response and for preparing the attachments. A few follow-ups from our network team:

- Single CIDR preference: we prefer a single /24 per region if possible to simplify firewall policies.
- PrivateLink vs peering: we are planning to use interface endpoints (PrivateLink) for control-plane API calls, and peering/transit for data plane in prod. We will need the DNS flow and any recommended TTLs for your interface endpoints so that our DNS team can plan overrides.

One ask: can you explicitly mark which egress IPs are used for telemetry/metrics vs. customer API traffic? We need to segregate telemetry traffic in our firewall rules.

If you can confirm the /24 availability and provide a short note about DNS TTL recommendations, we should be able to mark the SIG network section as "answered".

Thanks — Emily

(Quoted text below)
> On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 11:08 AM Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Emily — thanks for the clarity, happy to provide. Quick answers up front, followed by attachments and clarifying questions.

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@medarc.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Apr 2027 13:42:05 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence for private endpoints and peering

Emily — attaching the updated evidence pack per your asks and inline answers below. Attachments included: redwood_private_endpoint_ip_allowlist_v1.csv; vpc_peering_config_snapshot-20270405.txt; network_topology_medarc_private_endpoints_v1.pdf; egress-ip-range-summary.txt

Inline answers:
- Single CIDR: confirmed — we can reserve a dedicated /24 per customer per region when a reserved egress option is selected in the Private onboarding. We've flagged the ranges in redwood_private_endpoint_ip_allowlist_v1.csv with the "reserved" tag where applicable. For customers on ephemeral NAT we provide a small pool (usually /28 or /29) that rotates; those are untagged.

- Telemetry vs API traffic: the CSV includes a column "purpose" with values: control_api, customer_api, telemetry. See rows for 54.210.160.0/24 (control_api) and 34.212.23.0/26 (telemetry) as examples.

- DNS / PrivateLink: recommended TTL for DNS overrides is 60s for failover-sensitive endpoints (control plane) and 300s for non-critical telemetry endpoints. The topology PDF has callouts showing that control plane traffic should use interface endpoints with DNS override; data plane routing (customer inference traffic) is typically over peering/transit with route table entries on both sides.

- Peering snapshot: vpc_peering_config_snapshot-20270405.txt includes an exported route table example and a redacted peer config. Note: we have redacted account IDs and sensitive tags per internal policy.

If you need a signed attestation or a fabric-level pcap, we can schedule a short session with our network ops team — we avoid sharing raw pcaps in this phase but will produce sanitized evidence on request.

Let us know if this is sufficient to close the SIG network section or if you want us to open a secure share for additional artifacts.

Thanks,
Diego

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@medarc.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, it-security@medarc.com
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence for private endpoints and peering

Diego / team — this is great, exactly what we needed. A few next steps from MedArc:

- We will provision the /24 reserved ranges on our firewall list for staging and production (per-region) — thank you for confirming availability.
- Our DNS team will use the TTL guidance and will follow up if they need the specific CNAME override mappings for the PrivateLink endpoints.
- We're happy with the peering snapshot as redacted. If our auditors ask for a signed confirmation we may request a short attestation later; we'll ping you if that becomes necessary.

Closing the SIG network section now — I'll mark the SIG as answered in our tracker and share the updated questionnaire export.

Appreciate the quick help,
Emily
